t.2.48.1: Having spent the auspicious night at that great tree, they set out from that place when the sun had risen, clear and bright.
t.2.48.2: Plunging into a very great forest, they went, making for that region where the Gaṅgā, the Bhāgīrathī, flows toward the Yamunā.
t.2.48.3: The illustrious ones went over the land, seeing here and there various delightful regions they had never seen before.
t.2.48.5: Look, Saumitri, at the smoke rising up near Prayāga, the banner of the blessed Agni; I think the sage is close at hand.
t.2.48.4: They journeyed on in safety, and as the day was just ending, Rāma, gazing at the many kinds of trees, spoke to Saumitri.
t.2.48.6: Surely we have reached the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā, for indeed the sound of water dashed against water is heard.
t.2.48.7: Here wood split by forest-dwellers who live by it can be seen, and these trees of many kinds are seen at the hermitage of Bharadvāja.
t.2.48.8: Having journeyed on in ease, those two bowmen, as the sun was sinking low, reached the hermitage of the sage at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā.
t.2.48.9: Rāma, having reached the hermitage and startling the beasts and birds, went a short distance further and approached Bharadvāja.
t.2.48.10: Then, having reached the hermitage, the two heroes, followed by Sītā and eager to see the sage, stood waiting at a distance.
t.2.48.11: The moment he saw the illustrious one, who had just performed the agnihotra offering, Rāma, with hands joined in reverence, saluted him together with Saumitri and Sītā.
t.2.48.12: And the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa made himself known to him: "O venerable one, we two are Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the sons of Daśaratha."
t.2.48.14: When I was being banished by my father, this dear younger brother Saumitri, firm in his vow, followed me into the very forest.
t.2.48.13: This is my wife Vaidehī, the auspicious daughter of Janaka; blameless, she has followed me to the lonely penance-grove.
t.2.48.15: Commanded by our father, O blessed one, we shall enter the ascetic forest; there, living on roots and fruits, we shall practise dharma alone.
t.2.48.16: Having heard those words of the wise prince, the righteous one then brought forward a cow, the guest-offering and water.
t.2.48.17: The sage, seated amid beasts and birds and surrounded on all sides by ascetics, honoured Rāma who had arrived and addressed him with words of welcome.
t.2.48.19: At long last indeed, O Kākutstha, I see you come here; and I have heard of this banishment of yours, which is without cause.
t.2.48.18: When Rāghava had accepted that offering of worship and was seated, Bharadvāja then spoke to him these words, filled with dharma.
t.2.48.21: Thus addressed with these words by Bharadvāja, Rāghava, Rāma, who delighted in the welfare of all, replied with an auspicious speech.
t.2.48.20: This place at the confluence of the two great rivers is secluded, holy and delightful; may your honour dwell here happily.
t.2.48.22: O revered one, the people of the city and the countryside, being near at hand, will come here as onlookers to see Vaidehī and me as well. For this reason I do not wish to dwell here.
t.2.48.23: O blessed one, look for an excellent hermitage site in a secluded spot, where Vaidehī, the daughter of Janaka, who is worthy of happiness, may delight.
t.2.48.24: Having heard these auspicious words of Rāghava, the great sage Bharadvāja then spoke words that grasped their purpose.
t.2.48.25: Ten krośas from here, dear one, is the mountain on which you will dwell, frequented by great sages, holy, and pleasant to behold on every side.
t.2.48.26: Roamed by black-faced langurs and frequented by monkeys and bears, it is renowned as Citrakūṭa and resembles Gandhamādana.
t.2.48.27: As long as a man beholds the peaks of Citrakūṭa, he devotes himself to auspicious things and does not set his mind on evil.
t.2.48.28: There many seers, having spent a hundred autumns, ascended to heaven through their austerity, together with Kapālaśiras.
t.2.48.29: I consider that secluded dwelling a pleasant one for you; or else, Rāma, live here with me for your sojourn in the forest.
t.2.48.30: Bharadvāja, knower of dharma, received Rāma, his beloved guest, together with his wife and with his brother, and honored him with every object of desire.
t.2.48.31: For Rāma, who had approached that great seer at Prayāga and was telling many wondrous tales, the auspicious night came on.
t.2.48.32: When the night had given way to dawn, the tiger among men approached Bharadvāja and spoke to the sage of blazing splendor.
t.2.48.34: When that night had passed and dawn broke, Bharadvāja spoke these words: "Go to Citrakūṭa, rich in honey, roots and fruits."
t.2.48.33: Venerable one, O you of truthful conduct, today we have spent the night here in your hermitage; now may your honor grant us leave to settle in a dwelling place.
t.2.48.35: There, all around in the forest regions, herds of elephants and herds of deer roam about; those you shall see, O Rāghava.
t.2.48.36: Having reached that auspicious mountain, which resounds with the calls of joyful koyaṣṭikas and cuckoos and is made most delightful by frolicking deer and by many elephants, take up your dwelling in a hermitage.
